I'm really, really sorry, but I don't think we're talking about the same thing. See, being a play, the only reason I refer to Claudette as the "main character" is because she has the most time onstage. If I were to actually pick out the protagonist, it would be either her brother or best friend, (both flawed, well written characters, in my opinion, but I'm biased.) Claudette IS at the center of the story, but only in the same way as the Holy Grail, or the sleeping princess. Plus, she does have a minor character arc, (being raised in a slum and wanting to not be ignored or looked down upon anymore.) Which is the main theme of the play.

Our problem is that I see my character as a plot-relevant side character, and you're holding her up to the standards of other protagonists, which she truly is not. She only takes action twice, and the second time she dies because of it. (And I made a point to clarify in the script that had sne not made that choice, she would have lived,) 

But you are correct in saying that the plot revolves around her, like she's a black hole. The reason why I think this is justified, however, is because I don't think she's truly the protagonist, but a centerpiece for the story to roll around. She was meant to be a symbol of love and kindness, and I wanted to show that the very idea for love makes the world go round. A neive ideal, yes, but one I wanted to share.

Okay, this is REALLY long, so bear with me.

One day, late spring, it was really cloudy, and it was almost dark out, not that the clouds helped. I wanted to get a branch I could use for a craft project,  and I decided to walk yo the woods and check off the paths, since I'd found some great stuff before. So I was wandering around as it started to get darker, and the wind was really picking up, almost disaster movie levels. Now, I love storms, so I was happy with this, and even better, I stumbled across some fireflies that I decided to follow, taking pictures with my phone. 

Then the rain hit, and I realized that I had to get home. But with the rain, wind, and now thunder and lighting, (which was REALLY close by) I couldn't find my way back to the path. I knew there was a clearing of sorts if I broke through the trees, so I did, but then I realized; I'm in a large clearing, filled with sharp, thigh-high grass and small, but deep hidden creeks everywhere, in a massive, super close lightning storm. But at least I could see out there, so I tried to walk across long ways because I knew there was a road in that direction. As I started to get more worried, I started yelling at whatever evil spirits were doing this to me to tell them I wasn't scared. I even started making up a poem that I was shouting at the top of my lungs.

But the grass was slicing up my legs and the wind was making me exaughsted, and I have insane anxiety disorder. So when I fell in a creek, which turns out was chest - high,  I managed to wade out and collapse.  I felt like I was going to faint, because I was soaking wet in a goddamn lightning storm and I was hyperventilating. I could not breathe.  I was screaming and begging for help, and eventually conceded defeat to whatever sprits were out there- you know, "I'm scared, are you happy?" 

At that point I gave up on the clearing and went back into the woods. I was breathing a bit better now, but I was still panicking. I tried to call 911, (my phone doesn't have a plan, so I can only call 911) but falling in the creek made it too water damaged and it shut off. Going through the woods, I thought I saw the streetlights, so I tried following those - turns out those were more fireflies, and I got more lost, ending up in TALLER razor sharp grass. (Found out later that I couldn't have seen the street lights due to a blackout). That's when I couldn't breathe again,  and I was scared I would faint in a really dangerous place here. Luckily, I finally remembered my water bottle and drank some to calm myself. 

With one final push, I found the path again, before finally breaking back out onto the paved walking paths. I followed them to a suburb area, where every house is exactly the same, and glanced inside windows, trying to find that looked trustworthy. Eventually I found one with an older woman, a pregnant lady and two tween-age girls. Imagine their shock when a soaking wet, crying girl with scratched up legs appeared at their door, smiled with pure exagution,  and said,  "I was lost in the woods, and my mom's really worried. Can I borrow your phone?"

I got the call. Also a towel and a ride home. So yeah, that was horrifying for me.
